summary: Full backend + frontend E2E validation of the new MOD Auto Quote spreadsheet-import feature. Backend endpoint POST /api/crm/mod-quote/import-spreadsheet passed 5/5 pytest cases (paste text, CSV upload, missing input → 400, no-auth → 401/403, bad contract_type → 400). Frontend E2E: logged into CRM via UI (admin@pulsefitness.com), switched to Corporate mode, opened Quotes (CPQ), clicked MOD Auto Quote (data-testid mod-quote-btn) → wizard opened with dropzone visible; selected Contract A, used paste path with the sample rows; wizard advanced to Step 2 (toast: 'Recognised 4 item(s) — 3 matched, 1 to review'), AI-import note surfaced ('TOTALS row ignored as subtotal…'), 3 matched lines showed green '% match' badges (62%/60%/78%), Widget XYZ 9000 flagged 'needs review' with £0 price and no rate-card mapping, TOTALS/header rows correctly ignored. Clicked Review (mod-next-2) → Step 3 → Generate Quote (mod-generate-btn) → MOD quote MOD-20260806-7E87 created (subtotal £837.73, VAT £167.55, total £1,005.28) with the Widget line preserved at £0 as a needs-review line. Regression: existing 'Select MOD site + Load Equipment' path still present in Step 1 (mod-site-select + mod-next-1 rendered).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routes/crm_mod_quote.py _match_recognised(): 'suggestions' is referenced before assignment in the else-branch (line 315 defines it only when rc is not None from code match; when rc becomes non-None via keyword match the earlier branch never ran, so suggestions is undefined). In practice Python resolves it because Python uses function-scope binding and the else clause covers only the 'code hit' path, but the control flow reads awkwardly — recommend initialising `suggestions = []` at the top of the function.

backend/routes/crm_mod_quote.py import_spreadsheet(): no maximum size/row cap on the uploaded file before shipping the whole grid to the LLM. Consider capping content length to avoid runaway token spend on adversarial uploads.
Frontend CRMMODQuoteWizard.js (~532 lines) is approaching the 700-line guideline — RateCardEditor could be split into its own file for readability.
